questions.def: "Most" is a quantifier used to indicate the majority of a group.
questions.question: ___ of the students passed the exam with flying colors.

questions.def: "A large number of" is used with countable nouns like "people."
questions.question: ___ people attended the conference, which was a great success.

questions.def: "Few" emphasizes the small number, implying it's almost none.
questions.question: Surprisingly, ___ people knew the answer to the difficult question.

questions.def: "Little" is used with uncountable nouns like "time" to show scarcity.
questions.question: I have ___ time to finish the project; I need more.

questions.def: "Insufficient" means not enough; formal for uncountable "evidence".
questions.question: There is ___ evidence to support his claims.

questions.def: "Several" means more than two but not many. Often precedes 'of'.
questions.question: ___ of my colleagues are attending the workshop next week.

questions.def: "Much" is used with uncountable nouns like "cake" in this context.
questions.question: ___ of the cake was eaten, and it tasted delicious.

questions.def: "None of" indicates that zero employees are satisfied.
questions.question: ___ the employees are satisfied with their salaries.

questions.def: "Amount" is used for uncountable nouns like "money."
questions.question: A significant ___ of money was donated to the charity.

questions.def: "Few" means almost none and has a negative connotation.
questions.question: He has ___ friends living in this city; he feels lonely.

questions.def: "Further" implies additional information is needed.
questions.question: We need ___ information before making a decision.

questions.def: "Plenty of" means a lot of something, enough or more than enough.
questions.question: There is ___ of food in the refrigerator; you don't need to buy more.

questions.def: "Several" means more than two but not many; countable nouns only.
questions.question: ___ of the books on the shelf are missing their covers.

questions.def: "A few" implies a small number, but enough to be worth mentioning.
questions.question: Only ___ students submitted their assignments on time.

questions.def: "Majority" means more than half of a group.
questions.question: The ___ of voters supported the new legislation.

questions.def: "Some" is used with uncountable nouns like "information."
questions.question: ___ of the information provided was useful for the project.

questions.def: "Many" is used with countable plural nouns in negative statements.
questions.question: There aren't ___ buses running late at night.

questions.def: "Amount" is the correct quantifier for uncountable nouns like "sugar."
questions.question: A small ___ of sugar is enough for the recipe.

questions.def: "No" is used to indicate a complete lack of something (idea).
questions.question: I have ___ idea what you are talking about.

questions.def: "Much" is used with uncountable nouns like "money" in negative contexts.
questions.question: I don't have ___ money left after paying the bills.

questions.def: "Number" is used with countable nouns such as "birds."
questions.question: A large ___ of birds migrate south every winter.

questions.def: "Some" is used with plural pronouns like "us" to mean a portion.
questions.question: ___ of us are going to the party tonight.

questions.def: "Most" can be used directly before an uncountable noun like "fruit."
questions.question: ___ of the fruit in the basket was rotten.

questions.def: "Few" means not many and refers to countable nouns.
questions.question: ___ of the applicants had the required experience.

questions.def: "Little" refers to a small amount of uncountable nouns.
questions.question: There's ___ evidence to support his claim.

questions.def: "Number" is used with countable nouns like people.
questions.question: Only a small ___ of people attended the meeting.

questions.def: "A lot of" is used with both countable and uncountable nouns.
questions.question: He drank ___ water after the marathon.

questions.def: "Most" can be used without "of" before possessive pronouns.
questions.question: ___ of my friends are going to the concert.

questions.def: "Quantity" refers to an amount of something uncountable.
questions.question: A large ___ of effort is needed to succeed.

questions.def: "Several" means more than two but not many, for countable nouns.
questions.question: ___ students failed the exam, unfortunately.
